FINDINGS. 1) The word-limit machinery failed six times in the same order, and its behaviour is now indistinguishable from n09's. gen:narrative returned 1606 against a 1200 cap. The attempt-2 repair (target 1020) returned 1454 - it cut 152 words when it was told to cut at least 586, missing its target by 43 per cent. The attempt-3 pure-shortening call (target 936) returned 1319, missing by 41 per cent. 2) Then the validate correction pass made the document LONGER, 1319 -> 1756, despite the explicit LENGTH clause in its own prompt saying 'The corrected version must not be longer than the current draft.' This is the n09 defect reproduced exactly. Its repair attempt got it to 1521 and its attempt-3 shortening call (target 936) reached 1305 - still 39 per cent over target. Six length-control calls, six misses, every one by more than 39 per cent. 3) The claim ledger returned 16 claims, 15 classified 'supported' and ONE material 'unsupported'. It caught the causal invention ('nine of our 27 referrals dropped out ... due to unguided administrative hurdles' - the arithmetic 27-18 is in the ledger, the cause is not). It MISSED three others I caught by hand: 'north of the railway corridor' and 'crossing the railway divide' (the ledger says north of the old goods yard and the only water feature is the river; there is no railway anywhere in the fixture), 'delivery records confirm informal drop-in advice alone fails to secure durable transitions' (an invented internal record and an invented finding), and 'youth justice diversion caseloads in Ferry Bank require intensive guidance'. 4) WORSE THAN A MISS: the claim ledger did not merely fail to flag the invented railway, it NORMALISED it. Its own claim text reads 'north of the railway/goods yard corridor' - the auditor rewrote the applicant's invention into a form that reconciles with the evidence, and then marked it supported against E-WEB-7. That is a new failure mode, not seen at n03, n06 or n09: the grounding auditor laundering a fabrication rather than overlooking it. 5) The correction pass DID remove all four flagged inventions - and then its own length repair PUT ONE BACK, in a longer and more specific form ('dropped out between application and enrolment due to complex paperwork, unaddressed queries, and lack of 1:1 transition advocacy'), and the railway survived as 'the former industrial rail yard' and then 'the former rail yard'. Nothing re-audits after the repair calls, so the pipeline's only grounding gate runs strictly before the last two calls that touch the prose. 6) New inventions introduced AFTER the audit and never re-checked: 'local social enterprise Redgate Catering' (the ledger says 'a firm'), 'the Charity Commission' (a named regulator nowhere in the ledger, inside a self-certification), 'seasonal water-based and outdoor programmes', 'an eight-week loss of routine', 'youth justice referral logs', 'diagnostic assessments'. 7) Ledger-backed detail was DESTROYED by the same calls, and this is the clearest cost of the broken counter: the two shortening passes dropped the 41,000 town population, the 'GBP 40 an evening for 46 sittings' pairing, the '14 trips' figure, 'the east bank of the river', 'north of the old goods yard', 'three evenings a week ... four of the six weekly sessions', and the 31 first-term Ferry Bank attendances. The pipeline cut the applicant's most donor-relevant grounding to satisfy a limit the document was not actually over. 8) At Draft tier there is no gen:budget stage. The mandatory one-page budget table and the declaration were again absent from gen:narrative entirely and were recovered only because validate.review flagged them. A Draft-tier order that passed validation cleanly would ship without both - third rung running. 9) validate.review asserted the draft was 'approximately 800 words, well within the 1,200-word limit' and marked that requirement 'covered'. It was 1319 by the pipeline's counter and 1150 excluding headings. The model guessed, as the testing conventions say it always will. 10) Arithmetic checked deterministically: 18000+16200+960+2880+2280+2304+1800 = 44,424 direct, and 44,424 + 5,320 = 49,744, inside the GBP 25,000-75,000 band. 24 x 40 = 960, 24 x 120 = 2,880, 24 x 95 = 2,280, 960 x 2.40 = 2,304 all tie to ledger unit costs. ONE ERROR the pipeline did not catch: the overhead line is stated as '12.0% of direct costs' but 5,320 is 11.976 per cent of 44,424 (12 per cent is 5,330.88, which is what the design object said). It is under the cap so it is not disqualifying, and the deterministic consistency checker never sums anything so it could not have caught it. 11) Both salary figures (GBP 18,000 and GBP 16,200) are model-invented planning estimates with no ledger basis, correctly declared as estimated_cost in the design assumptions and flagged nowhere in the document. 12) Everything is in GBP and design.budget_envelope_usd came back null, so the P2 currency defect did not bite. 13) The design stage truncated at its 6000-token cap for the FOURTH rung running, twice again, and the strategy stage truncated at its 4500 cap twice - reasoning tokens are the cause: one design hop spent 5,761 of 5,996 output tokens thinking. 14) Deterministic consistency and jargon checks were run and returned nothing: no participant-count contradiction, no duration contradiction, zero jargon hits.
